title: Prime Numbers
statement: Given an integer n, return true if it is a prime number, otherwise return false. A prime number is greater than 1 and divisible only by 1 and itself.
think: What is the task asking? Check whether the number has any divisor other than 1 and itself.
What is the key operation? Test divisibility using the modulo operator.
What wording signals stand out? Prime, divisible, factors.
Which pattern fits? Linear Scan, because we scan possible divisors.
What is the brute force idea? Try every number from 2 to n - 1.
What is the better/optimal idea? Try divisors only up to sqrt(n).
What are the edge cases? n <= 1, n = 2, even numbers.
What is the complexity? O(sqrt(n)) time and O(1) space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I check divisors from 2 up to sqrt(n), and if any divides evenly, the number is not prime.
algorithm: Loop i from 2 while i * i <= n
If no divisor is found, return true
interview: I would solve it by checking divisors from 2 up to the square root of n. If any divisor divides n evenly, the number is not prime; otherwise it is prime.
ru: Нужно проверить, есть ли у числа делитель кроме 1 и самого числа. Если есть — число не простое.
visualExplanation:
n = 17
i = 2 -> 17 % 2 != 0
i = 3 -> 17 % 3 != 0
i = 4 -> stop, because 4*4 > 17
no divisor found -> prime

important: Loop all the way to n instead of stopping at sqrt(n)
nice: Do not explain why sqrt(n) is enough

gaps: Nice to have: explain sqrt optimization
whyThisPattern: This is a linear divisor-checking problem: we iterate over possible divisors until we either find one or finish.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Dictionary, because there is no counting or mapping.
Not Two Pointers, because there is no left/right sequence traversal.
